content.title: About
content.content: An alcoholic coffee drink combines aromatic coffee with a spirit such as whiskey, rum, or brandy. It can be served hot or cold, often with cream, sugar, or spices, and is popular both in bars and home preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first known recipe for an alcoholic coffee appeared in Europe in the 17th century.
In Italy, the popular "caffè corretto" is espresso with a splash of grappa.
In the United States during the 1930s, Irish coffee (coffee with Irish whiskey and cream) became a post‑war staple.
Some recipes use flavored liqueurs such as amaretto or Kahlúa for extra taste.
Alcoholic coffee is often served in special glassware to highlight its color and aroma.

items.title: Stimulation and relaxation
items.content: Caffeine boosts alertness while moderate alcohol can promote relaxation, creating a unique balance.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coffee is rich in polyphenols, and certain spirits (e.g., brandy) contain phenolic compounds that may act as antioxidants.

items.title: Warmth in cold weather
items.content: A hot alcoholic coffee helps warm the body and improves circulation in chilly conditions.

items.title: Caffeine‑alcohol interaction
items.content: The combination can mask the feeling of intoxication, increasing the risk of over‑consumption.

items.title: Blood pressure increase
items.content: Caffeine may temporarily raise blood pressure, and alcohol in larger amounts can amplify this effect.

items.title: Caffeine intolerance
items.content: People sensitive to caffeine should limit their intake of the drink.

content.title: How to Make
content.content: Brew a strong fresh coffee (espresso or filtered). Add 30‑50 ml of your chosen spirit, sweeten to taste (sugar, honey, or syrup), and stir. Optionally top with whipped cream, cinnamon, or grated chocolate. Serve hot or chill and serve over ice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The drink is prepared just before serving, so it does not require storage. Keep spirits in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool, dark place, and store ground coffee in an airtight container protected from moisture and light.
